title: How interactive-demo works
subtitle: Record your product, write it up, ship it on your own page.

widgets.title: A demo of your product, made from your product
widgets.description: Click through your app once. The CLI records every click as a step, a local editor lets you write it up, and the result is a folder you can drop on any page — or one link you can send.

image.alt: A terminal running the capture command

steps.label: Record a click-through

background.alt: A terminal running interactive-demo capture start and capture stop

steps.script: capture start opens Chrome and arms a recorder. You click through your product the way you would show it to a customer, then capture stop writes the demo into your project.

annotations.text: One command opens Chrome and starts watching your clicks. `capture stop` writes the steps to disk.

steps.label: See what you got

background.alt: The local preview playing the captured demo

steps.script: interactive-demo dev serves the demo straight away. Nothing was mocked: this is the product, screen by screen, with a pointer wherever you clicked.

annotations.text: The pointer lands where you clicked, so a viewer follows the path you took.

steps.label: Write it up

background.alt: The editor with the demo open, the step strip on the right and the annotation toolbar below

steps.script: The editor runs on your machine and saves to demo.config.json as you work. Add a message, move a hotspot, cut a step you did not need.

annotations.text: Every captured screen is a step. Reorder them, retitle them, drop the ones you did not need.

steps.label: Get the snippet

background.alt: The editor's Share dialog showing the publish commands and a field for the link

steps.script: Share hands you the exact commands to publish, then fills the embed snippets in with your link. No account is needed to build and host the folder yourself.

annotations.text: Paste your published link here and the Inline, Popup and React panes fill their snippets in with it.

steps.label: Build it

background.alt: A terminal running interactive-demo validate and build, listing the output folder

steps.script: build writes one self-contained folder per demo: the page, the player, your screens. Nothing in it depends on where you serve it from.

annotations.text: One self-contained folder per demo — or one command to a hosted link.

steps.label: Put it on the page

background.alt: The demo running inline on a marketing page

steps.script: The inline snippet is an iframe sized to the demo's own ratio, so it never letterboxes. The framed player relays its events to the page around it.

annotations.text: The same folder, sitting in a page: no bar, no chrome, just the demo.

steps.label: Or open it over the page

background.alt: The demo opened in a pop-up over the site's hero

steps.script: The pop-up is one script tag and a button. It takes the demo's aspect ratio, locks the page behind it, and closes on Escape.

annotations.text: Any button on your site can open it: InteractiveDemo.open(url).

widgets.title: Record, write up, ship
widgets.description: Everything you just saw was recorded from a running app by the capture command in this repo, written up in the editor, and built into a folder. The tour you are watching is that folder.

image.alt: The finished demo opened over a marketing page
